contracts.invariant: A retry publishes the captured source only when its explicit destination lease and remote settings still hold.
contracts.rootCause: Retries rebuilt from mutable branch/configuration state can overwrite work or change destinations.

tests.oracle: Read the actual bare remote ref and require the captured source OID.
Read the bare remote before and after both fetch timings; the newer OID must survive.
Configuration drift refuses retry without replacing the captured plan.

contracts.invariant: Literal refnames, custom tracking mappings and named-remote hooks retain their identity.
contracts.rootCause: Interpreting plus/equal characters as refspec operators or reconstructing a remote loses Git semantics.

tests.oracle: Inspect destination refs after a real push of a literal leading-plus branch.
Inspect effective mapping and remote ref for a branch containing equals.
Observe hook remote identity and the configured receive-pack execution.

contracts.invariant: An operation accepts at most one begin and one terminal event; stale callbacks cannot reactivate it.
contracts.rootCause: Duplicate, reordered and cancellation callbacks can publish twice or replace a newer journey.

tests.oracle: Accepted event log retains the first user choice.
All event sequences through length four preserve public lifetime invariants.
Declining recovery completes through the actual failure event.

contracts.invariant: Git path identity is exact bytes, distinct from display strings and Unicode equivalence. Symbolic worktree HEAD references retain exact UTF-8 identity and remain complete inventory records; only refs/heads/ targets project local-branch behavior, while non-local targets browse the captured commit.
contracts.rootCause: Lossy decoding, BOM stripping and Swift String equality collapse or redirect paths. Restricting porcelain branch fields to local branches rejects valid tag, remote and custom symbolic HEADs; reconstructing from the local projection loses their reference identity.

tests.oracle: Require literal Unicode and BOM byte round trips.
Compare raw Data keys across record rotations, duplicates and display collisions.
Resolve actual selected path and parent rather than its rendered label.
Literal Git history excludes matching decoy paths while object reads remain correct.
Working-tree and staging image lookups preserve the explicit stage-zero identity of a colon filename after actual staged selection.
Actual staged and unstaged selections render the correct labels and return the exact index and worktree image bytes.
Actual selections preserve unmerged index diff sections and dangling symlink targets.
Selecting a staged colon filename renders an expanded image from the index on the renderer queue.
One mixed inventory preserves local, detached, bare and valid tag/remote/custom symbolic records instead of rejecting the whole snapshot.
The legacy initializer retains local branch semantics but keeps full non-local symbolic titles without granting branch identity.
An isolated reciprocal-link fixture survives reconstruction with exact symbolic reference presentation and filesystem flags.
The independent real Git check-ref-format oracle accepts full references and rejects malformed components without normalizing the parser input.
Compare exact UTF-8 Data for composed/decomposed refs and explicit-versus-legacy constructor inputs, keeping local branch projection separate.
The value policy retains local unborn references and emits captured commit identities/descriptions only for nonempty, nonzero symbolic or detached heads.
Malformed, contradictory, duplicate and invalid UTF-8 records still reject the complete inventory after valid non-local references are admitted.
Isolated real Git tag, remote and custom symbolic HEAD output remains complete through parsing and reciprocal-link inspection without changing refs or checkouts.

The native commit list and settled history text render a commit reachable through a non-local symbolic checkout using the captured full OID, while lifecycle menus and exact HEAD/ref proofs remain correct.
Compare literal adjacent punctuation byte sequences with real Git beside combining marks, keeping non-adjacent pairs valid and preserving raw identities.
Real Git tag and remote symbolic HEADs remain lifecycle-only worktree rows, preserve the normal reference rows and disable branch remote controls without changing refs or HEADs.

contracts.invariant: Every selected path is validated before any mutation; raw identities never become shell/display text. Queued worktree locate repair revalidates the captured folder and administrative ownership at writer admission, preserving both repositories' links when either identity changes.
contracts.rootCause: Partial validation and pathspec metacharacters can mutate the wrong files or leave a partially applied selection. Validating a locate folder only before queueing allows a replacement folder or reused administrative name to inherit mutation authority.

tests.oracle: Inspect exact NUL input, literal flags and capability probe count.
Actual raw-byte files are addressed; invalid selection causes no mutation.
No chunk launches after an unsafe capability/selection combination.
An unchanged folder admitted after a held writer gains the exact administrative backlink and Git directory, while its actual HEAD remains unchanged.

Replace the queued folder with another repository's worktree; compare exact .git, backlink, HEAD and index bytes, both repositories' refs, and the foreign checkout HEAD after refusal and subsequent queue release.
Recreate the administrative directory under the same name while repair waits; refusal preserves the replacement backlink and selected folder's exact .git bytes.

While locate repair waits, replace a missing sibling registration's folder with a foreign checkout without changing administrative evidence; refusal preserves both .git files, administrative backlink, HEAD and index bytes, actual checkout HEADs and refs, then releases the queue.

While repository-wide repair waits, a missing sibling folder reappears as a foreign checkout; unchanged administrative evidence grants no authority to overwrite it, and exact links, HEAD and index bytes, actual checkout HEADs and refs survive refusal and queue release.
Captured original-folder ownership permits repairable missing or malformed links and rejects foreign targets, ambiguous registrations and malformed administrative backlinks.

A captured target rejects changed .git bytes, administrative backlinks or common links, replacement checkout or registration identities, and unreadable evidence while unchanged ownership remains valid.
A valid managed .git symlink remains browsable while automatic repair refuses to replace its object and preserves the exact symlink destination.

A readable stale .git symlink is not advertised as automatically repairable; refusal preserves the symlink object and destination, target identity and bytes, administrative links, HEAD, index and checkout content.

A moved checkout with a readable stale .git symlink retains its exact move identity and refuses automatic replacement while preserving the symlink, target bytes, registration metadata and tracked content.

With unchanged saved .git bytes, a previously missing target becomes a real foreign registration while Locate or repository-wide repair waits; re-resolution refuses mutation, preserving both repositories' links, administrative metadata, HEAD, index, content and refs, then releases the queue.

A captured stale .git target becomes an existing foreign directory without changing saved link bytes; validation and fresh capture reject it while the selected checkout identity and exact administrative fingerprint remain unchanged.

A selected .git link keeps its exact bytes while its Git-directory alias is retargeted; validation and fresh capture refuse while the raw link, administrative fingerprint and new alias destination remain unchanged.

An administrative backlink keeps its exact bytes while its path alias is retargeted to a different checkout; validation and fresh capture reject it, fresh fingerprint evidence changes and no longer matches the registered checkout path, and the backlink bytes and new alias destination remain unchanged.

An administrative common link keeps its exact bytes while its path alias is retargeted to a foreign common directory; validation and fresh capture refuse, fresh fingerprint evidence changes and no longer matches the registration ownership, and the common-link bytes and new alias destination remain unchanged.

Administrative fingerprints freeze the resolved endpoint of a backlink independently of its raw bytes; retargeting the checkout's managed .git symlink changes fresh evidence while captured and fresh fingerprints still attribute the same checkout path and registration identity.

Retarget a moved checkout directory alias while global repair waits; Git repairs the captured canonical checkout rather than the alias's new foreign target, preserving foreign links, metadata, HEAD, index, content and refs while the owned checkout becomes the published registration with its exact administrative backlink.

Capture owned and missing Git-directory targets through alias/.. paths, then retarget the alias without changing .git bytes; queued validation must reparse the saved bytes and reject the changed target resolution rather than trusting the normalized target captured earlier.

contracts.invariant: Only the current mutation generation and comparison identity may publish a refresh or authorize a hunk; whole-file discards must revalidate the selected discardable files. List transactions publish one complete ordered selection of raw bytes and staging sides. Unchanged selection preserves capture; genuine selection changes and the exact caller raw-path set control discard authority. Background worktree discovery restores sidebar selection without replacing content mounted by an inspector or presenter. Prune authority is bound to the approved preview's administrative registrations and revalidated at writer admission; changed candidates require an updated preview and a new confirmation. Sidebar row restoration refreshes controls and preserves local-branch reference actions without changing mounted content or the browsed revision. Worktree callbacks and deferred confirmations retain their originating window, repository, service and presentation generation; closing or replacing an owner revokes authority even when the same objects are restored. Expected cancellation is silent while genuine current-owner failures remain observable.
contracts.rootCause: A stale callback or cached action can replace a newer selection or apply obsolete content. A prune confirmation detached from current registration identity can forget worktrees the user did not approve. Restoring a row without its selection notification leaves controls stale; treating worktree rows only as lifecycle actions loses retained reference actions. Rebuilding an action from current owners or checking visibility alone lets old callbacks and deferred clicks regain authority after replacement or reopening.

tests.oracle: Index reconciliation finishes between stage and unstage, with tracked and Unicode paths preserving mutation order.
The next intended selection remains observable after staging.
A later user selection survives the delayed operation callback.
A real index publication makes the old action refuse mutation.
Confirmation completion revalidates current content before applying.
Tracked contents are restored and the untracked binary remains byte-identical.
Real NUL-delimited Git output authorizes a tracked raw-byte deletion without text decoding.
Each changed confirmation input rejects authorization before mutation.
Decomposed filename bytes authorize a real Git hunk discard.
Diff remains visible with no mutation token when image identity is unavailable.
Unstage exactly the selected hunk while retaining the other staged hunk and all worktree bytes.
Hold actual capture across real list callbacks in both layouts; unchanged refresh selection succeeds, while changed bytes, side, deselection, closure, or a state message cancels.
Refresh, filtering, sorting, layout changes and mixed sectioned selection publish complete selections; split exclusivity holds before each callback.
Reordering the same byte paths and sides cancels the held capture.
Close prevents a pending coalesced render from starting Git commands.
Fixture deletion waits for validation enqueued by earlier main callbacks to complete on the writer.
Missing, extra, differently scoped raw paths launch no mutation; equivalent reordered sets use frozen ordered bytes.
A real image lookup from an earlier render refuses bytes after refresh or deselection; an unchanged selection update preserves its read.
Explicit branch selection returns real mounted content to history while preserving checkout HEAD; the existing general reload behavior remains observable.
A real sibling-worktree change publishes a snapshot while mounted content, viewed branch, selected branch, and checkout HEAD remain unchanged.
Calling the legacy destructive prune entry point without a captured preview refuses the operation and preserves the actual administrative registration.
Make another worktree prunable after preview; refusal preserves both real administrative directories and allows the following queued writer to complete.

A changed candidate set replaces the real confirmation sheet before any registration changes; cancellation preserves both backlinks and checkout HEADs, and a fresh approved preview then deletes its registrations while preserving the moved folder and main HEAD.
The native inspector stays visible at cold launch; explicit confirmation fetches only the approved ref and switches to the named branch at the approved OID.

Exact administrative fingerprints change for HEAD, lock, common-link and backlink bytes or replaced registrations, retain identity across index/log changes, and require a one-to-one match with registered paths.
Unsupported .git object classification retains the moved path that blocks prune, without advertising automatic repair or changing the managed link and registration evidence.

Explicit repair and prune actions present a manual-repair notice with no mutation buttons for the moved managed .git symlink; exact link targets, registration metadata, actual HEAD and refs remain unchanged.

Administrative fingerprints freeze the resolved endpoint of a backlink independently of its raw bytes; retargeting the checkout's managed .git symlink changes fresh evidence while captured and fresh fingerprints still attribute the same checkout path and registration identity.

Retarget a captured administrative common-directory alias while prune waits, keeping raw link bytes, revision OID and candidate report identical; a renewed preview is required and both repositories' exact metadata and refs survive before the following queued operation completes.
Both actual sidebar menus retain routed branch actions, dispatch Copy after construction returns, include each lifecycle selector once, and preserve real HEADs and refs.

Upstream configuration changes absent to present to absent at both rebuild boundaries update actual controls while canonical selection, mounted alternate content, the revision object, porcelain, refs and both HEADs stay unchanged.
Hold the shared writer, externally unlock, and require the later real Git error in the live origin plus exact ownership/content preservation and following-writer reconciliation.
Cancel the queued origin while its window remains visible; no mutation or error presentation occurs and the following real writer finishes.
Closing and reopening the retained window cannot revive the queued callback; captured links and content survive and the following writer finishes.
A real held Git rejection across repository or window A-to-B-to-A replacement never presents in the restored owner and releases the shared writer.
An accepted forced-removal click dispatched after owner replacement cannot acquire a writer or remove dirty contents, while the next writer succeeds.
A held raw Git report cannot display a preview after owner replacement/restoration; registrations survive, the next preview matches real report bytes, and a fresh journey remains available.
A real right-click popup exposes retained branch actions and the safe Open Worktree substitute; its current screenshot precedes activation of the correct existing checkout, preserving both HEADs.

After hiding an unchanged supported owner, preparation and confirmation failures from real Git never present; following previews finish, registrations survive, and a fresh visible journey remains available.

contracts.invariant: Successful chunks are reconciled before controls recover, including failure paths. Busy commit submissions refuse immediately without enqueuing, while background Git commands retain FIFO order.
contracts.rootCause: Early return or premature idle publication leaves the displayed index and operation eligibility untruthful.

tests.oracle: Observe parsed components and main-thread completion.
Inspect actual staged first chunk and reconciled UI after second-chunk failure.
Controls recover only after authoritative reconciliation, preserving hook failure.
A duplicate click during reconciliation produces one staging result and no error notification.
A synchronous checkout is refused while the shared repository writer owns a staging operation.
Busy menus and stale reference/stash invocations preserve HEAD, worktree and stashes; a real Git failure still presents its error after admission recovers.
Hold the writer queue before execution; synchronous work is refused without running, queued completion releases ownership, and the coordinator accepts the next write.
Reconciliation and submission each reject a main-thread writer without launching it while read output remains available.
Before releasing the held writer, observe exactly one refusal, no hook or commit-message write and unchanged HEAD; retry after idle commits the original message.
The existing background Git command still executes after previously queued staging.

contracts.invariant: Prepared retries preserve HEAD identity, parents, message, signing and environment except the chosen verification policy.
contracts.rootCause: Retrying from refreshed state changes user intent; equal OIDs alone miss branch identity changes.

tests.oracle: Observe hooks, resulting message and HEAD publication.
Compare every captured field and the only allowed verification change.
Distinguish actual symbolic, detached and unborn identities despite matching OIDs.
Cancellation and launch failures permit another probe; successful capability evidence remains reusable.
Changed merge markers survive post-publication cleanup.
Invalid UTF-8 and malformed merge parents refuse publication and retain captured state.
A gated probe coalesces identical executable requests while a different executable completes.
An explicit unsupported protocol result launches once across repeated requests.

contracts.invariant: Immutable-copy actions reject selections containing Working State; text drags reject a clicked Working State source without changing the pasteboard.
contracts.rootCause: Menu-only validation leaves direct responder actions and mixed drag selections unguarded.

tests.oracle: Compare actual multi-commit formatting and empty-selection output.
Invoke real responder actions and require unchanged clipboard text.
With Working State as the clicked source, test every text column and Working State/mixed row selection; retain pasteboard generation and types.

contracts.invariant: Root, ordinary and merge patches preserve final tree content and a final byte without a newline.
contracts.rootCause: Incorrect diff parent/format or line chopping creates unusable or incomplete exports.

tests.oracle: Apply and am exported patches with real Git; compare final tree IDs.
Compare exact final content when output has no final LF.

contracts.invariant: Completion preserves exit status and accepted bytes, while genuinely incomplete drainage stays explicit.
contracts.rootCause: Leader exit is mistaken for EOF; arbitrary reader cutoffs truncate finite streams or hide descendant output.

tests.oracle: Compare complete bytes from slow finite readers.
Observe descendant output released after the parent exits.
Repeated drainage cannot upgrade an incomplete stream to complete EOF.
A controlled peer exit between reads preserves its final acknowledgement.
The failure reason retains diagnostics written just before exit.
Injected application resource failures preserve caller descriptors and the successful control reaps its child.
Only a positive syscall write makes commit publication uncertain.

contracts.invariant: Rendered and exported diagnostics redact credentials across every chunk/cutoff boundary while preserving ordinary URLs.
contracts.rootCause: Truncating before redaction or parsing only common userinfo shapes can expose secrets.

tests.oracle: Ordinary URLs and subsequent diagnostics remain byte-faithful.
Every two-part split excludes the credential from output.
Both summary cutoff and full export exclude secrets.
Malformed userinfo stays redacted through the application boundary.
Dotted usernames and numeric password prefixes remain hidden across chunks.

contracts.invariant: An export error survives temporary invisibility and is discarded only after actual owner dismissal.
contracts.rootCause: Visibility is confused with lifetime, causing lost errors or presentation on a closed owner.

tests.oracle: Observe actual owned artifact, destination and restored control.
Hide/minimize then restore; exactly one error is presented.
Closed or detached owners receive no later error.

contracts.invariant: Tests and explicit-checkout Git inspection isolate inherited repository selectors while retaining configured local hooks and binary input.
contracts.rootCause: Ambient repositories, config, hooks and identity make tests pass against the wrong state.

tests.oracle: Inspect isolated Git environment and preserved non-Git variables.
Real Git commits preserve explicitly configured fixture hooks.
Compare exact binary stdin bytes.

contracts.invariant: Required Objective-C selectors and Swift consumers remain valid in both build configurations; Objective-C-imported subclasses can execute controller callbacks without Swift-only virtual dispatch failures.
contracts.rootCause: Conditional runtime/test surfaces or bridge annotations compile in Debug but fail in Release; new Swift-only virtual state accessors can have missing dispatch slots in Objective-C-imported subclasses.

tests.oracle: Invoke the window delegate through an Objective-C-imported subclass and preserve both nil-window and loaded-window state without crashing or presenting a repair sheet.
Query required Objective-C selectors in the running Debug host.
Exercise the imported task and configuration-dependent runtime surface in Debug.
Exercise the imported task and configuration-dependent runtime surface in Release.

A nib-backed loadWindow probe stays at zero across owner setters and Objective-C-imported callbacks; explicit KVO delivers the real repository change through the existing layout barrier, and showWindow provides a positive load control.

contracts.invariant: UI fixture repositories ignore untracked Finder metadata while preserving real untracked files, explicitly tracked metadata and existing exclusion rules.
contracts.rootCause: Finder-created .DS_Store files alter first-file selection, dirty counts and before/after status oracles.

tests.oracle: Real Git status still reports a modified tracked .DS_Store and ordinary untracked source.
Inject root and nested Finder metadata; real Git status retains only real files, including a similarly named notes file.
Preserve existing rule bytes and Git ignore/negation behavior; repeated setup keeps the same exclusion file.
Repeated policy setup preserves exclusion bytes even with a trailing unrelated rule or no final newline.
Linked worktree status ignores metadata using the resolved Git exclusion location.
A clone automatically receives metadata exclusion through the shared creation boundary.
